issue.title: SASE_FEATURE_FLAGS pins an agent runner to the launcher's flag resolution, so a scope:"project" flag would resolve against the wrong project
issue.description:
PROPOSED BY: phase bead sase-nb.2 (2026-08-16T16:49:43Z) during epic sase-nb ('Feature flags whose removal is a bead, a deadline, and a gate'); triaged and filed by the sase-nb land agent at close.

PROBLEM: epic decision 7 exports the launching process's fully resolved snapshot into SASE_FEATURE_FLAGS. src/sase/feature_flags/env.py:76 encode_feature_flags_env() serializes every decision's final boolean, and apply_feature_flags_env() writes that string into the child environment. An agent runner launched from ACE therefore inherits the ACE process's resolution -- which was computed against the launcher's config layers, not the agent workspace's project-local config -- instead of resolving for itself.

WHY IT IS DORMANT TODAY: both registered flags are scope:"global" (src/sase/feature_flags/registry.py:34,45), and src/sase/feature_flags/resolver.py:95 rejects a local-config override of a global-scope flag outright ('scope_violation'). So there is currently no flag whose correct value can differ between the launcher and the launched workspace, and the pinning is unobservable.

WHY IT NEEDS A DECISION: the scope field exists precisely so a flag can be overridden per project (docs/configuration.md documents scope:"project" as locally overridable). The first scope:"project" flag makes the inherited snapshot wrong for any agent whose workspace config disagrees with the launcher's, and the failure is silent -- the child never re-resolves, and sase.doctor.checks_flags only flags inherited env values as a warning (src/sase/doctor/checks_flags.py:259).

SCOPE: decide and implement one of -- (a) encode only scope:"global" decisions into SASE_FEATURE_FLAGS and let the child resolve project-scoped flags itself; (b) carry the launcher's project identity alongside the snapshot so the child can tell whether the pin applies to it; or (c) declare the pin intentional and make it explicit (reject scope:"project" flags at registration, or fail loudly when a child's project differs). This must be settled before the first scope:"project" flag ships, not after.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-nb — the closed epic that shipped the registry, the SASE_FEATURE_FLAGS transport, and epic decision 7. Phase sase-nb.2 proposed this; the land agent verified it is dormant only because both shipped flags are scope:"global".
